newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END MIXED IN DULL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END MIXED IN DULL TRADE.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished mixed after dull trade on Friday after strong gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were offset by widening backwardation, traders said.

"Three months (on the LME) scored more gains. But Tokyo futures don't look as attractive because of backwardation," said one trader. "As before, people are still watching the precious metals market, which is in turmoil."
The June contract climbed 1.7 yen to 203.8 yen per kilo, while the April shed 0.5 yen to 205.2 yen. Others were up between 0.5 and 1.1 yen. Estimated volume was a thin 1,427 lots.
In London overnight, the benchmark three-month aluminium powered higher to touch $1,775 per tonne, its highest level highest since October 9, 1995, before finishing at $1,762.5.
